title: File exceeds 1000 lines (1209 lines total)
detail: utils.py contains 1209 lines of heterogeneous utility functions covering time arithmetic, file caching, RPC helpers, and thread-locking primitives. Growing catch-all utility modules accumulate unrelated concerns and become difficult to navigate. Suggested fix: group functions by concern into sub-modules (e.g. utils/time.py, utils/fileutils.py).

title: 8 `datetime.datetime()` calls without `tzinfo` in `last_completed_audit_period` and `last_completed_audit_period`
detail: Ruff DTZ001 flags 8 calls to `datetime.datetime(...)` without a `tzinfo` argument across lines 162–214 in `last_completed_audit_period` and the surrounding helpers. Naive datetimes in a cloud API that serves multi-timezone deployments can produce incorrect audit windows when UTC offset changes (DST) or when timestamps from different time zones are compared. Suggested fix: pass `tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc` to each constructor, or use `datetime.datetime.now(tz=datetime.timezone.utc)` / `timeutils.utcnow()` consistently.

title: `try: lock.release_write_lock() except Exception: pass` silently swallows lock-release failures
detail: Lines 1103–1105 attempt to release a write lock in a `finally`-style context and silently ignore any exception. If `release_write_lock()` raises, the lock may remain held, causing subsequent threads to deadlock when they try to acquire it. Suggested fix: at minimum log the exception; consider whether the lock's type guarantees idempotent release or whether the call should be guarded by a condition (e.g. check if the lock is actually held).

title: Redundant exception object in `logging.exception` call
detail: Line 1016 passes the exception as an explicit argument to `logging.exception(...)`, which already captures and formats `sys.exc_info()` automatically. The duplicate argument causes the exception message to appear twice in the log output. Suggested fix: remove the exception variable from the `logging.exception` call arguments.
